paradoxes.text: Ocean of Peace rejects militarisation and great-power rivalry, yet Fiji's security depth is becoming Australian (Vuvale treaty talks, police embedded with the AFP, an RFMF company inside an Australian Army brigade): the closer Canberra comes, the less the 'no great power' message reads as neutral to Beijing and to Pacific states that resist Australian primacy, and the declaration was criticised for sidestepping regional issues.

grand_strategy.reading:
Rabuka's Fiji takes the Pacific frame as its own instrument: it chairs the Melanesian
Spearhead Group, carried the Ocean of Peace through the Forum and opened an embassy in
Jerusalem, while selling security to Canberra and Wellington and seeking money and tariff
relief from Washington. The open question is whether a no-alliance posture survives a
Vuvale treaty, closer policing with Australia and a general election due at the turn of
2026-27.

stances.note: Ally since 6 Jul 2026 (review correction, mirrored from Australia's card with the same sources): Albanese and Rabuka signed the Vuvale Union and the Ocean of Peace Alliance (Veitacini Treaty) in Suva, which DFAT lists as Fiji's first alliance and Australia's fourth; the text was finalised on 8 May 2026 after the Wong-Conroy visit and CSIS leaves open whether it limits Fiji's security engagement with China. Before that: the Vuvale Partnership elevated in July 2025, treaty talks opened at the Defence Ministers' Meeting in Suva on 3 Oct 2025, AFP officers inside the Fiji police, a 2025-29 package of about A$500m. Warming: each step larger than the last. Bond - affinity: Pacific and Commonwealth ties, not kinship.

stances.note: Partner under the Duavata Partnership, with a 2023 framework for military cooperation on each other's territory; NZ Police officers work in the Fiji Police Partnership Program (third group arrived January 2025). Rabuka and Luxon met on the sidelines of the Honiara Forum in September 2025, and NZ backed the Ocean of Peace. The partnership was renewed in Auckland on 16 July 2026 for five years, signed by the foreign ministers, with a target of NZ$2bn two-way trade by 2030. Stable because renewal is routine. Bond - affinity: shared Pacific identity and the Duavata term, not kinship.

stances.note: Partner, transactional. Cooling on aid: the 2025 State Department freeze named a US$1.5m clean-energy programme run by the SPC Fiji office, and Rabuka went to Washington in February 2025 to ask it to reconsider the freeze and to rejoin the Paris Agreement. Warming on trade: the US reciprocal tariff on Fiji-origin goods was 32% in April 2025, cut to 15% from 8 August 2025, then ended with the IEEPA ruling in February 2026; the Foreign Ministry says Fijian exports are no longer under the Section 122 surcharge that expired in July 2026, while some calculators still show it. A Zero List negotiation is open. Stable because the two push opposite ways. Bond - none.

stances.note: Partner, not reluctant partner: the cooperation is transactional (fisheries, police training) and Fiji resists Chinese officers inside its force, not alignment itself. Cooling: in January 2023 the Rabuka government moved to end the 2011 police MoU; the Home Affairs Minister then said it was under review with six months' notice, and by March 2024 Chinese officers stationed in Fiji had been ruled out, short-term deployments ended and intelligence sharing curtailed, while the MoU itself stayed in force under six-monthly review. Rabuka cited Australia and NZ as partners with comparable systems (SCMP). A 2025 Chinese-side release says more than 100 Chinese vessels use Fiji as a base; it is promotional and tier 4. No 2025 high-level China-Fiji contact was found in this pass. Bond - none: pure interest.

stances.note: Partner with kin: Rabuka's first visit to India as PM (24-26 August 2025, talks at Hyderabad House on 25 August) rested on a 2017 defence memorandum and a first Joint Working Group on Defence (peacekeeping, military medicine, white shipping data). India is opening a defence attache post in Suva, plans a naval port call and a 100-bed super-speciality hospital. Warming. Bond - kin: Indian officials say almost a third of Fijians trace their roots to India (indenture from 1879); Hindi is an official language. Modi did not visit Fiji in 2025; the last Indian PM visit reported in the sources is 2014 (not sourced in a row). Trade is lopsided and the figures conflict (see the USD 65m row).

stances.note: Partner, transactional, from the former colonial power: Fijians have served in the British Army since the 1961 recruiting drive, and the UK remains a top source of tourists (UK arrivals up 10.6% in 2025). No treaty and no alignment. Stable. Bond - affinity: Commonwealth membership and a shared colonial past, with no open grievance. Headcounts of Fijians in the British Army are contested and undated, so none is used here. The since date (1970, independence) is not sourced in this pass and should be checked.

relations_from.summary: US reciprocal tariff on Fiji-origin goods: 32% in April 2025 (the highest in the Pacific, on a US claim of 63% duties on US goods that Fiji disputes), cut to 15% from 8 Aug 2025. The IEEPA duties ended on 24 Feb 2026 and a 10% Section 122 surcharge expired on 24 July 2026; the Foreign Ministry says Fijian exports are no longer under it, while some calculators still show it. A Zero List negotiation is open.
relations_from.note: Fiji's own average import duty on US goods is under 2%, per the Fiji side. Some third-party tariff calculators conflict with the Foreign Ministry's July 2026 statement; the government statement is the more recent source.

relations_from.summary: Vuvale Partnership elevated in July 2025 (Albanese and Rabuka): development assistance of about A$500m for 2025-29, including an extra A$40m over four years; AFP officers working inside the Fiji police; A$12m for container screening at Lautoka and Suva. At the Defence Ministers' Meeting in Suva on 3 Oct 2025 both sides agreed to start negotiations toward a treaty, and a 20-year maintenance MoU and Guardian-class boats were confirmed. One Fiji Sun headline gives A$734m for the package; to check.

relations_from.summary: Rabuka in Tokyo, 12-13 Nov 2025: a summit with PM Takaichi on 13 Nov that created the Japan-Fiji Lomavata Kizuna Partnership, marking 55 years of relations; Defence Minister Koizumi received him, and Fijian cadets have entered Japan's National Defense Academy. The two defence ministries date the courtesy call differently (11 or 12 Nov).

He urged the US to rejoin the Paris Agreement.

relations_from.summary: Fiji's embassy in Jerusalem opened on 17 Sep 2025, with Rabuka and Netanyahu at the ceremony at Israel's Foreign Ministry, making Fiji the first Pacific island state to open an embassy there. Fiji had abstained on a recent UN vote calling for Palestinian statehood. In October 2025 Deputy FM Haskel's visit to Fiji produced a digital security and cybersecurity memorandum with Israel's National Cyber Directorate.
